name: Vietnam

facts.religion: Folk religion and no religion about 85%, Buddhist, Catholic minorities

snapshot: To Lam, re-elected party chief in January 2026 and now also president, has become Vietnam's most powerful leader in decades while slashing the bureaucracy.
culture: Vietnam's culture draws on Confucian, Buddhist and Taoist traditions, and Tet, the lunar new year, is the year's great family festival. Pho, banh mi and street coffee culture are national treasures. Ancestor worship is practised in most homes. Water puppetry, performed on ponds in the Red River delta, is a centuries-old art.
society: Vietnam has been one of the world's fastest-growing economies, with Samsung, Apple suppliers and others moving factories there from China. The Communist Party tolerates no opposition. A sweeping "blazing furnace" anti-corruption campaign has brought down top leaders, and in 2025 the government merged provinces and cut tens of thousands of state jobs.
situation: Since the 1980s, Vietnam's Communist Party has avoided strongman rule by sharing power among "four pillars": the party chief, the president, the prime minister and the head of the National Assembly. That model helped turn one of the world's poorest countries into a manufacturing powerhouse. In 2026, To Lam, a former police chief, broke it.

On 23 January the party's 14th Congress re-elected Lam as general secretary, and analysts said he was poised to become the country's most powerful figure in decades (NPR). In April he also took the presidency, the first Vietnamese leader elected to both jobs for full terms since 1986 (The World This Wiki/Economist digest). As public security minister, Lam ran an anti-corruption campaign that removed two presidents and many rivals. Now he wants speed: the congress set a target of at least 10 percent annual growth through 2030, aiming to make Vietnam a high-income country by 2045. The economy grew about 8 percent in 2025, but Lam himself called the target "tremendously challenging" with Vietnam dependent on exports facing a 20 percent US tariff. He has slashed the bureaucracy, merged provinces, and declared an "era of national rise," while keeping "bamboo diplomacy" between Washington and Beijing.
power: A one-party communist state. The Communist Party's Politburo and its general secretary set policy; the National Assembly, almost entirely party members, elects the president and prime minister.
holders: To Lam, general secretary and president; Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh.
